headline: JDE Peet's deal lifts sales, one-offs crush GAAP profit
summary_short: Keurig Dr Pepper's Q2 FY2026 net sales rose 75.6% y/y to $7.309 billion on the JDE Peet's acquisition, while GAAP diluted EPS fell 90.0% to $0.04 from $0.40 a year ago; Adjusted diluted EPS rose 16.3% to $0.57.
summary_long: Net sales grew 75.6% to $7.309 billion (74.6% constant currency); legacy KDP (ex-JDE Peet's) grew 7.3% on price and volume/mix gains. GAAP operating income fell 30.1% to $628 million on comparability items including a $314 million JDE Peet's inventory step-up and higher intangible amortization; Adjusted operating income rose 42.9% to $1.478 billion. GAAP net income attributable to common shareholders fell 89.0% to $60 million ($0.04 diluted EPS); Adjusted diluted EPS rose 16.3% to $0.57. Operating cash flow was $895 million and free cash flow $714 million for the quarter. KDP reaffirmed FY2026 guidance: net sales of $25.9-$26.4 billion and low-double-digit constant-currency Adjusted EPS growth, targeting a 4.1x pro-forma leverage ratio by year-end.

drivers.explanation: Growth was driven by the JDE Peet's acquisition (closed April 1) plus 7.3% organic growth in legacy KDP, itself from 4.2% net price realization and 3.1% volume/mix gains.
Decline was primarily driven by an unfavorable year-over-year swing in items affecting comparability, including acquisition and integration-related costs tied to the JDE Peet's deal.
EPS decline is arithmetically consistent with the 89% net income decline above, diluted over a slightly higher share count and after the new preferred-stock allocation.
Growth tracked the Adjusted operating income increase, tempered by higher Adjusted interest expense, non-controlling interest allocations, and earnings allocated to preferred holders.

Decline reflects an unfavorable year-over-year swing in items affecting comparability, including a $314 million JDE Peet's inventory step-up and higher intangible amortization per the reconciliation table.
Growth came from top-line gains, productivity savings, and the JDE Peet's contribution, tempered by inflation and heavier marketing-led SG&A spend.

CEO Tim Cofer said Q2 EPS topped expectations, with U.S. Refreshment Beverages posting double-digit growth and KDP International improving as planned; the company reaffirmed full-year 2026 guidance while progressing on JDE Peet's integration and the planned early-2027 separation.
